summary: The morning risk-off call (confidence 0.5) ran straight into the oversold bounce I listed as the main risk. The SPY benchmark in close.json rose from 539.98 to 565.41, about +4.7% on the day, which puts SPY near 722, back above the ~690 level in my first watch item and roughly 1% under its 730.28 200-day. For a risk-off grade SPY now has to fall more than 1% below the 689.81 reference over the remaining four sessions of a holiday-shortened week. That means giving back the whole bounce and then some, so this call will probably grade wrong. The book gained only 3.63 (about +0.6%) at 47.6% invested against the shadow's 99.4%. The 'duration and cash only' framing cost participation: TLT was +0.15% on the day, while the single stocks the account still holds rose about 1.2% to 2.8% (KR -1.9% was the exception).
broken_theses: 'The only things worth owning here are duration and cash.' On the first session TLT added +0.15% while SPY rose about 4.7%. The hedge did no harm, but cash and duration were the worst places to be on a relief day.

'New equity risk should wait for a stabilizing week rather than try to catch the bounce.' The bounce came on day one, before any stabilizing evidence could show up in the packet. With 20-day vol at 26.55% against 14.39% over 252 days, a one-day move this size was within reach and I gave it too little weight in the stance itself. I put it only in the watch list.

Second time this pattern has failed: the 11-06 risk-off call, made right after the 11-05 Nasdaq selloff, graded wrong at +2.59%. Today's call, made after a -8.56% SPY week, looks headed the same way. Two cases are not a rule, but extreme 5-day drops have been the weakest setup for my risk-off calls, while the 11-12 and 11-13 risk-off calls made earlier in the decline graded right.
update: At the next run, read the new packet before moving. The 5-day window will still carry the 11-16 to 11-20 selloff, so its numbers will look worse than the tape now is. Check my own watch triggers: VIXY 5-day turning negative with SPY above about 690 (the SPY half is now met), and RSP reclaiming its 200-day (it was only 0.34% below). If both hold, move to neutral at least. Go to risk-on only if SPY's 21-day trend and HYG also improve, because SPY is still under its 200-day and the regime filter stays defensive-only until it closes above about 730. Neutral is not a safe harbor at this volatility (a 1% band is small against 26.55% 20-day vol), so choose a direction if the evidence points one way. My process note for future calls: when SPY's 5-day return is near -8% and 20-day vol is roughly double the 252-day, hold risk-off confidence at or below 0.4, or don't add to it, because the relief-rally risk is symmetric with the trend risk. Treasuries are still the right regime-allowed defensive sleeve, but I would not ask for further duration adds on the strength of one week's hedge.
